title: Types
explain: Go is statically typed, and `:=` declares a variable and infers its type inside functions. Basic types include `int`, `float64`, `string` and `bool`, and every variable starts at a zero value like `0` or an empty string. Constants declared with `const` cannot change.
code:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	var count int // zero value: 0
	name := "Ada" // inferred string
	const pi = 3.14159
	price := 9.99 // float64
	fmt.Println(count, name, pi, price)
	fmt.Printf("%T %T\n", name, price)
}
exercise: Declare an int, a float64, a string and a bool, print them with `%T`, then try adding the int to the float64 and read the error.
tip: Go refuses to compile unused variables and imports. Use `_` to discard a value on purpose.
